slides.headline: Her parents sold curtains from a market stall in Leicester. In 2026, their daughter became Britain's Ambassador to the Vatican.
Tammy Sandhu presented her credentials to Pope Leo XIV on August 28, 2026, as the UK's Ambassador to the Holy See
slides.body: She became the first woman from an ethnic minority background - and the first woman of Indian origin - to hold the post, confirmed by an official Vatican Press Office record of the credentials ceremony.

slides.headline: Born and raised in Leicester, England, to parents who migrated from Punjab in the 1960s, she joined the UK Foreign Office in 2005.
slides.body: Her parents worked market stalls selling household goods before starting a family business. She went on to serve as HM Consul General in San Francisco and in postings including Chennai, Rabat and Brussels.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when the children of its emigrants end up representing other nations at the world's oldest diplomatic institutions.
slides.body: Sandhu's own words capture it best: "I only wish my parents were able to see where I am today."
